historyReviewBoundary: All 115 histories have author source checks. Final independent review covered metadata and numerical checks for all 115 classes, 12 deeper class targets and source-gap samples in seven classes. It did not independently verify every passage of every cited source.

history.name: Angiotensin II receptor blockers

starting.description: Takeda researchers observed diuresis from synthetic CV-2198, then blood-pressure lowering at doses without diuresis. On investigating this effect they found angiotensin II antagonism in rabbit vessels and developed related antagonists including CV-2961. DuPont built on weak, selective antagonism of related Takeda benzylimidazoles. Angiotensin II physiology and prior peptide antagonists supplied the biological context.

inspiration.description: CV-2198's diuretic and non-diuretic blood-pressure effects led to a demonstrated synthetic angiotensin antagonist series. The renin–angiotensin system and endogenous angiotensin II supplied biological context and a later molecular-modeling reference.

steps.description: Angiotensin II physiology and peptide antagonists provided biological context and exposed limitations for chronic therapy.

Takeda observed diuretic and independent blood-pressure effects of CV-2198, investigated the mechanism and found angiotensin II antagonism; related structure–activity work produced CV-2961. A 1982 patent reports angiotensin II antagonism by imidazole-acetic acid derivatives in rabbit vessels and rats.
DuPont evaluated two patented Takeda benzylimidazoles and observed weak selective competitive receptor antagonism, despite not confirming the reported potency.
Peptide-guided lead enlargement and structure–activity work generated more potent but orally inactive phthalamic acids, orally active biphenyls and the tetrazole-containing losartan.
Further Takeda work on benzimidazole acids and ester prodrugs led to candesartan and candesartan cilexetil, with a changed ring system and improved oral delivery.

Later class designs retained a relation to the losartan prototype while changing the active architecture, including an amino-acid-derived replacement of the imidazole in valsartan and an imidazolinone in irbesartan.

After oral losartan was reported, Sankyo screened synthesized imidazoles and optimized a potent, long-acting lead into olmesartan; its medoxomil ester was selected to improve oral availability. An earlier paper's abstract reports testing of related acids and oral esters.

design.description: Researchers separated diuresis from antagonist effects, modeled synthetic antagonists against endogenous angiotensin II, and changed structures to improve affinity, selectivity, oral activity and duration. Later benzimidazole, imidazolinone and amino-acid-derived active structures represent architecture changes, while esterification of candesartan and olmesartan was a prodrug delivery change.

circumstances.description: The investigation of CV-2198's blood-pressure effect, subsequent antagonist structure–activity studies, and DuPont lead optimization were deliberate. Whether the initial diuretic or blood-pressure finding was unexpected is not established by the retrospective.

limits: S1 documents the DuPont losartan line; S2 documents Takeda's early lead work and related candesartan branch. S4 relates irbesartan and valsartan to the losartan prototype and describes their different architectures, not their entire individual invention histories.
S5 gives Sankyo's later observation-and-optimization route to olmesartan in a one-page meeting summary. It does not establish the full chemical genealogy or priority for each analogue.
S2's crucial p. 803 account is in Japanese. The translation used here has not received an independent language check.
conflicts: S1 reports that DuPont could not confirm the potency claimed for the Takeda compounds; the account nonetheless reports weak selective competitive antagonism.
gaps: The 1982 patent reports antagonist experiments but not the CV-2198 chronology; Takeda's 1991 laboratory reports have not been read, and the early diuretic-to-antagonist sequence is from a 1995 discoverer retrospective.
For the Sankyo branch, the 1996 original medicinal-chemistry paper's abstract was read but its full text was not; detailed lead-by-lead chemistry is not independently reconstructed.
